items.title: Getting started
items.text:
Welcome to the documentation for KubeScope Monitoring Dashboard.

This project is built around Kubernetes's Go client, which allow clients to query data from the API server.

items.title: Features
items.text:
This project is still a WIP, new features will be added regularly.

  • Cluster Overview – Nodes, namespaces, and workload status

  • Workload Monitoring – Deployments, Pods, ReplicaSets, and more

  • Events - Detailed event information inside the cluster

  • User-Friendly Interface: Intuitive UI for navigating and analyzing metrics.

items.title: Connects to API Server
items.text:
The back-end uses a client that communicates directly with the Kubernetes API Server using a service account with RBAC permissions.

No additional agents are required on worker nodes, except for kubelet itself.

items.title: Collect cluster data
items.text:
The client queries the Kubernetes API and retrieves data such as:

  • Nodes

  • Pods

  • Workload (Deployments, ReplicaSets, DaemonSets)

  • Network Services

  • Events

The back-end then exposed these data using a RESTful API layer for Front-end to fetch.

items.title: Visualization
items.text: The front-end fetches data from back-end and visualize them in a clean, organized Web UI.

items.title: Deployment
items.text:
There are 2 options to install KubeScope to your cluster:

  • Using Helm, with the project repository chart (recommended)

  • Using kubectl apply, with raw YAML manifests

items.title: Prerequisites
items.text:
Make sure you have the following installed:

  • Kubernetes cluster (v1.30+ recommended)

  • kubectl configured

  • Helm (optional)

items.title: Using Helm
items.text:
If you have Helm, you can start by cloning the repository.

git clone https://github.com/TonyQ-Lab/kubescope-dashboard.git

Move to the project's directory, and install the chart to a namespace of your choice.

helm install kubescope charts/kubescope -n kubescope-dashboard --create-namespace

Access the web interface.

kubectl port-forward svc/kubescope-frontend 8080:80 -n kubescope-dashboard

Now you can open your browser at http://localhost:8080 to view your dashboard.

items.title: Using YAML manifests
items.text:
Clone the repository, and move inside the manifest directory. 

git clone https://github.com/TonyQ-Lab/kubescope-dashboard.git

cd kubescope-dashboard/manifests

Creating a new namespace. 

kubectl create ns kubescope-dashboard

Create RBAC resources, these include ServiceAccount, ClusterRole and ClusterRoleBinding. 

kubectl apply -f rbac

Install dashboard components and its services. 

kubectl apply -f deployment -f service
